rows.text: # Mendel's laws of inheritance — monohybrid and dihybrid cross ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Mendel's laws of inheritance — monohybrid and dihybrid cross** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Heredity and Evolution fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Gregor Mendel (1822–1884), a monk in Brno, bred garden peas (*Pisum sativum*) from 1856–1863 and published in 1866. Peas were the right organism: true-breeding varieties, seven clearly contrasting traits, short life cycle, large numbers of offspring, and easy self- plus cross-pollination. He counted thousands of offspring and used mathematics — the first quantitative study of heredity.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Monohybrid cross scaffold: TT × tt → all Tt (F1) → F2 3:1 (phenotype), 1:2:1 (genotype) — draw the Punnett square; the ratios ARE the marks.  ·  Trick 2: Dihybrid: TtYy × TtYy → 9:3:3:1 — quote the law of independent assortment for the ratio; test cross with a double recessive gives 1:1:1:1.

rows.text: Trick 3: Three laws in one line each: dominance (one allele masks), segregation (alleles separate in gametes), independent assortment (genes on different chromosomes assort freely).  ·  Trick 4: Test cross identifies an unknown genotype: with a homozygous recessive, all-dominant offspring → parent homozygous; 1:1 → heterozygous.  ·  define + example each sub-idea: mendel's laws of inheritance — monohybrid, dihybrid cross.
